n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: The rains do not come. Week after week the sky stays white and the wind brings dust instead of clouds.

n2.speaker: amara
n2.text: The water table is dropping. The boreholes are sucking air half the time. Our pumps are giving half what they did.

n3.speaker: tendai
n3.text: Then we go deeper. It costs, but a deeper borehole keeps pumping when the shallow ones fail.

n4.speaker: narrator
n4.text: Click a pump and deepen its borehole. In an emergency you can truck water in, but it is expensive.

n5.speaker: tendai
n5.text: And keep the rangers close. Dry years bring hungry people, and worse than hungry people.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A letter on thick cream paper, delivered by hand.

partner.speaker: victor
partner.text: Dear partner. A drought like this ruins small reserves. Sell me the northern land and the lodge stays full, whatever the weather. Think of it as insurance.

cold.speaker: victor
cold.text: You asked about a pump. I have thought about that question a great deal. Sell me the north, and nobody needs to ask any more questions. You have one month.

plain.speaker: victor
plain.text: I am offering a generous price for the northern land, before the drought makes it worthless. My offer stands for one month.

end.speaker: tendai
end.text: The north. Of course he wants the north. Ask yourself why, {player}.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The rangers radio in at dawn. You find them standing around a carcass, hats in their hands.

n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: Shot. They took what they came for and left the rest to rot. And look around it.

n2.speaker: narrator
n2.text: Dead vultures lie in a ring around the body. A dozen at least.

n3.speaker: amara
n3.text: Poison. They lace the carcass so the vultures die before they can circle. Circling vultures tell rangers where a kill is.

n4.speaker: amara
n4.text: And without vultures, carcasses rot where they lie. That is how disease spreads through a herd.

n5.speaker: tendai
n5.text: Rangers in every zone that matters. And eyes on the fence lines: cameras, day and night.

n6.speaker: narrator
n6.text: Assign rangers to zones (Staff, H) and build camera posts on the marked spots (Build, B). Caught poachers and camera footage both count as evidence.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: Got one. Wire, a rifle with no serial number, and a phone full of numbers. That is evidence, {player}.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Kito is waiting by the gate before sunrise, hood up, looking over his shoulder.

friend.speaker: kito
friend.text: Tendai was kind to me. So I will tell you. All of it.

scared.speaker: kito
scared.text: They let me out on bail. I should not be here. But my mother says Ruth once paid for her hospital, so I owe you this.

tell.speaker: kito
tell.text: It is not hungry men from the village. It is a ring. Trucks, rifles, buyers overseas. They pay boys like me to carry and keep quiet.

n4.speaker: kito
n4.text: The trucks come in on the east road with no lights. The same road, the same trucks, as the night the old pump died.

n5.speaker: tendai
n5.text: They cut the pipe so Ruth would run dry and sell. And when she would not, they waited for her to die.

n6.speaker: kito
n6.text: The man who pays the drivers wears good shoes. They call him Mr H.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The northern fence is mended. Beyond it lies the wildest land in the reserve.

n1.speaker: amara
n1.text: There. By the thorn thicket. Do not move.

n2.speaker: narrator
n2.text: A black rhino steps out of the bushes, ears swivelling. Behind her, half-hidden, a calf.

n3.speaker: tendai
n3.text: A mother and calf. Now we know what Hale wants with the north.

n4.speaker: tendai
n4.text: Rangers up here, {player}. As many as we can pay for.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: In the night, thunder. By morning the dry riverbeds are running brown and loud.

n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: Rain. I had started to forget the smell of it.

n2.speaker: amara
n2.text: The grass will come back fast now. We held on. That is what matters.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The silver car is at the gate again. This time Victor Hale does not get out until you walk over.

n1.speaker: victor
n1.text: My offer expires today. I am told you have been collecting photographs. And a boy’s story.

n2.speaker: victor
n2.text: Photographs fade. Boys change their stories. Land is forever. Sign, and we can both forget all this.

choices.text: Hand everything to the police. All of it.
Sell him the north. Take the money and keep quiet.
Refuse, and seal the reserve: fences, patrols, nobody in or out without our say.

expose.speaker: narrator
expose.text: Three days later the police stop a truck with no lights on the east road. Two days after that, they come for Victor Hale.

n5.speaker: tendai
n5.text: Ruth would have liked to see that. So would I. I did, actually.

deal.speaker: victor
deal.text: A sensible decision. My lawyers will be in touch.

n7.speaker: tendai
n7.text: I hope the money keeps you warm, {player}. It will not keep that rhino alive.

lock.speaker: narrator
lock.text: Within a month the reserve is ringed in new wire. The poachers stay out. So does everyone else.

n9.speaker: wanjiru
n9.text: Our children used to walk to school along that road. Now they walk around your fence.

end.speaker: narrator
end.text: The silver car leaves for the last time.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: The pumps are only giving half. Click a pump and deepen its borehole before the waterholes go dry.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: We need proof that will stand up in court: caught poachers, camera footage. More rangers in the zones they hit, and cameras on the fence lines.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The drought is over. The wire is quiet. From the tower, at dusk, the visitors fall silent.

rhino.speaker: narrator
rhino.text: A black rhino walks down to the waterhole to drink, her calf close behind.

n2.speaker: amara
n2.text: Do you know how many people will never see that? And we get to see it from our own tower.

loss.speaker: narrator
loss.text: The waterhole is empty of rhinos. The poachers got there first.

n4.speaker: amara
n4.text: We will keep looking. Rhinos have walked in from the north before.

end.speaker: tendai
end.text: Ruth built this place to last. Whatever comes next, {player}, it will be your choices people remember.
